what_this_measures: ICLR 2026 main-text page budget compliance for paperC, and unreferenced-float defects, both derived from the build artifacts of the round_03 snapshot.

method.page_count: count LaTeX shipout markers (regex '\\[\\d+ ... \\]') in main.log BEFORE the position where main.bbl is read. The bbl is read exactly when \bibliography executes (main.tex:32), so markers before it == pages of main text (incl. the Ethics Statement, which precedes it).
method.why_not_pdf: this host has NO pdftoppm/gs/mutool/PyMuPDF, so pages cannot be counted by rendering; and grepping the PDF for '/Type /Page' returns 0 because the pages live in compressed /ObjStm (a bug already hit once and recorded in SKILL_LOCAL.md 3).
method.unreferenced_floats: for every \newlabel in main.aux, count \ref/\autoref/\cref/\Cref occurrences across sections/*.tex

why_the_build_gate_missed_the_unreferenc: latexmk reports 0 undefined references because every \label EXISTS. An unreferenced label is the OPPOSITE failure -- a float the prose never points the reader to -- and no LaTeX warning covers it. paper_build.py counts undefined refs, not unused ones.
consequence_for_revision: The over-length is ~1 page and 8 of 11 tables are unreferenced. These interact: the cheapest compliant fix is to move unreferenced main-text tables to the appendix and add explicit \ref for the ones that stay. This deletes NO evidence -- it relocates it -- so it does not weaken any claim. Recorded in decision_log.md.
not_verified: the exact page on which the main text would end after relocation (must be re-measured by rebuilding, not predicted)

whether ICLR 2026's CFP excludes the Ethics Statement / Reproducibility Statement from the 9 pages. The .sty carries no such text (grepped: 0 hits for 'page limit'/'ethics'). If they ARE excluded, the overage may already be smaller than 1 page. This must be checked against the official CFP before the fix is sized.

CORRECTION_20260815_MAIN.what_was_wrong: The first version of this file reported pages_main_text=10 and total=18, over_by=1. BOTH were undercounts.
CORRECTION_20260815_MAIN.root_cause: My shipout regex '\[\d+\s*(?:<[^>]*>\s*)*\]' was applied to the RAW log. TeX hard-wraps the log at ~79 columns, so a shipout marker whose bracket contains long embedded font paths gets a NEWLINE inside it and the pattern fails to match. Dropped markers -> undercount.
CORRECTION_20260815_MAIN.how_it_was_caught: The log's own authoritative line 'Output written on main.pdf (19 pages, 342809 bytes)' disagreed with my 18, and grep showed a literal '[19]' present. A self-inconsistency between my derived number and the tool's own report is the signal.
CORRECTION_20260815_MAIN.corrected_method: flatten the log (remove ALL newlines) BEFORE matching, then take the maximal monotonically-increasing marker run 1..N.
CORRECTION_20260815_MAIN.why_this_matters: the overage is 2 pages, not 1 -- twice what I first recorded. Sizing the fix from the wrong number would have under-cut and left the paper non-compliant.
CORRECTION_20260815_MAIN.generalisable_lesson: Never derive a count from a wrapped log with a pattern that can straddle the wrap; and when the tool reports the same quantity itself, cross-check against it before recording.
